steps.title: Import React
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file so you can use JSX and create components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Component will go here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React imported and ready to use for creating components with JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React. This gives you access to JSX syntax and React's component system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import statement. Make sure you're importing React from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like the correct import. You need to import React from the 'react' package to use JSX and create components.

steps.title: Create a functional component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Greeting that takes props as a parameter and returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should accept props as its parameter and return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Greeting component is defined that accepts props and returns null.
successCriteria: Greeting component is defined as a function that takes props and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Greeting component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Greeting component accepts props and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Greeting that takes props and returns null.

steps.title: Add JSX structure to the component
steps.instruction: Inside your Greeting component, return a JSX structure: a <div> containing an <h1> element that displays a greeting message using props.name.
steps.hint: The component should return JSX. Use props.name inside curly braces within the <h1> to display the name passed as a prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component returns a <div> with an <h1> that uses props.name to display a greeting.
successCriteria: The Greeting component returns JSX containing a <div> and an <h1> that uses {props.name}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added JSX structure to your component, making it ready to display a greeting using props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component returns a <div> with an <h1> that uses {props.name} to display the greeting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't yet return the required JSX structure. Ensure it returns a <div> containing an <h1> that uses props.name.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the Greeting component as a default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The Greeting component is exported using 'export default Greeting'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the Greeting component. This makes it available for use in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name 'Greeting'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't exported yet. Use 'export default Greeting' to make it available for import in other files.

steps.title: Create a defaultProps object
steps.instruction: Add a defaultProps property to the Greeting component and set the name prop to 'Guest'.
steps.hint: After the component definition, assign an object to Greeting.defaultProps with a name property set to 'Guest'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now has a defaultProps property that provides a default value for the name prop.
successCriteria: Greeting.defaultProps is defined as an object with a name property set to 'Guest'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added defaultProps to the Greeting component. This ensures the component has a fallback value when no name prop is provided.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've set the name property to 'Guest' inside the defaultProps object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure you're adding a defaultProps property to the Greeting component with the correct structure.

steps.title: Test the component without passing props
steps.instruction: Render the Greeting component without passing any props to see the default value in action.
steps.hint: Add the component as a self-closing JSX tag inside the return statement of your App component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component will be rendered without any props passed to it, allowing you to see the default prop values in action.
successCriteria: Greeting component is rendered as a self-closing JSX tag without any props passed to it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the Greeting component without passing any props. This will let you see the default prop values in action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering the Greeting component as a self-closing JSX tag without any props.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to render the Greeting component without passing any props to see the default values.

steps.title: Test the component with custom props
steps.instruction: In the App component, render the Greeting component a second time, passing a name prop with a custom value like 'Alice'.
steps.hint: Add another <Greeting /> JSX element inside the div, but this time include a name attribute with a custom string value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: rendering a component with custom props
<Button label="Submit" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now renders two Greeting components: one using default props and one with a custom name prop.
successCriteria: A second Greeting component is rendered inside the App's div with a name prop set to a custom string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the Greeting component with a custom prop. This demonstrates how custom props override default values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a second Greeting component inside the div with a name prop like name="Alice".
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added another Greeting component with a custom name prop inside the App's return statement.

steps.title: Add a second prop with default value
steps.instruction: Add a 'message' prop to the Greeting component's parameter list and set a default value for it in the defaultProps object.
steps.hint: Add 'message' to the props parameter and update the defaultProps object to include a default message string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component now accepts a 'message' prop with a default value defined in defaultProps.
successCriteria: The Greeting component's props parameter includes 'message' and the defaultProps object contains a 'message' property with a string default value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a second prop with a default value. This extends the component's flexibility while maintaining sensible defaults.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added 'message' to both the props parameter and the defaultProps object with a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. The goal is to add a 'message' prop to the component and provide a default value in defaultProps.

steps.title: Update JSX to use the new prop
steps.instruction: Inside the Greeting component, update the JSX to display both the name and message props.
steps.hint: Access props.message in your JSX, similar to how you access props.name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Greeting component will display both the name and message props in its JSX output.
successCriteria: The JSX includes both props.name and props.message, and the component returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated the JSX to display both props. The Greeting component now shows the name and message with their default values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying both props.name and props.message in the JSX. Check that your component returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The JSX doesn't seem to display both props correctly. Remember to access props.message in your JSX, similar to how you access props.name.

steps.title: Test with partial and full props
steps.instruction: In the App component, render the Greeting component three times: once without any props, once with only the name prop set to 'Alice', and once with both name='Bob' and message='Have a great day!'
steps.hint: Add three Greeting components inside the div. The first should have no props, the second should have name='Alice', and the third should have both name='Bob' and message='Have a great day!'
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: rendering a component with different props
<MyComponent />
<MyComponent color="red" />
<MyComponent color="blue" size="large" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display three Greeting instances showing how default props fill in missing values: 'Hello, Guest!' with 'Welcome to our site!', 'Hello, Alice!' with 'Welcome to our site!', and 'Hello, Bob!' with 'Have a great day!'
successCriteria: The App component renders three Greeting components: one with no props, one with name='Alice', and one with both name='Bob' and message='Have a great day!'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully demonstrated how default props work with different combinations of provided props. When no props are given, both defaults are used. When only name is provided, the default message appears. When both props are provided, the custom values override the defaults.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have exactly three Greeting components: one with no props, one with name='Alice', and one with both name='Bob' and message='Have a great day!'
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. In the App component, add three Greeting components inside the div: one with no props, one with name='Alice', and one with both name='Bob' and message='Have a great day!'
